title: Moving averages: the smoothed trend
desc: A 50-day average smooths price into one line, and it always lags

cards.title: Above or below?
cards.situation: A stock trades at $62. Its 50-day moving average is $55 and rising. What does that suggest?

chart.label: Price at $62 above a rising 50-day average at $55

options.text: The trend is up: price is above a rising average
options.feedback: Price above a rising average: the trend is up. It doesn’t say how long it lasts.

options.text: A crash is near: it’s too far above
options.feedback: Price above a rising average is what an uptrend looks like. Far above can mean stretched, but it’s no crash signal.
The average isn’t random: it’s the last 50 closes smoothed into one line. Price above it, with the average rising, shows the trend.

cards.title: The smoothed trend
cards.text: A **[[moving-average|50-day moving average]]** is the average close of the last 50 days. Each day it adds the newest close and drops the oldest. The wiggles shrink and the trend shows.

chart.label: Wiggly price with a smooth rising average under it

blocks.tip: Above a rising average: uptrend. Below a falling one: downtrend.

cards.title: It’s always late
cards.text: An average is built from past prices, so it turns after price does.

chart.label: Price turns down first; the average turns several days later

cards.foot: A slow average gives fewer false turns but reacts late. A faster one, like a 20-day, reacts sooner but flips more often.

cards.title: Use it as a filter
cards.text: Use the 50-day to decide **which side** to look at, not when to click. Price above a rising average? You look at buys only. Below a falling one? You wait.

cards.title: Work it out
cards.q: The last five closes were $10, $11, $12, $13 and $14. What’s the 5-day moving average?

options.feedback: $10 is just the oldest close. The average adds all five and divides by five, so it lands in the middle.
Add the five closes and divide by five. In a steady rise, the average sits below the latest price.
$14 is just the latest close. The average adds all five and divides by five, so in a rise it sits below price.
$60 is the sum of the five closes. Divide it by five to get the average.

cards.title: Barely moved
cards.q: Price fell 15% in two weeks, but the 50-day average has barely dipped. Why?

options.feedback: Nothing is broken. The 50-day spreads over 50 closes, so 10 new ones barely move it.

options.text: It spreads over 50 days, so two weeks count for little
options.feedback: Two weeks is about 10 trading days. Mixed with 40 older closes, they move the 50-day average only a little.

options.text: Price is about to bounce back
options.feedback: The average says nothing about a bounce. It moves slowly because 10 new days are mixed with 40 older ones.
A moving average uses closing prices, not the highs. It moves slowly because 10 new days are mixed with 40 older ones.

cards.headline: You can read the trend through the noise.
lines: A moving average smooths price into one line.
Above a rising average: uptrend. Below a falling one: downtrend.
It lags: it turns after price does.
